reason: The cited evidence shows Mo-oxide films (MoO2/MoO3) can reduce friction in Mo-containing HEAs, but it does not support the key premises that Mo stays in solution at room temperature, that the oxide can be controlled to be thin and adherent, or that the mechanism works across the full RT–800 °C range. E2 even describes oxide spallation and abrasive debris, contradicting the premise of a stable, adherent film.
premises: Mo addition to CoCrFeNi forms lubricious MoO3 tribofilm during high-temperature sliding
MoO3 tribofilm reduces friction and wear by providing easy shear and surface protection
Mo remains in solid solution at room temperature, preserving mechanical properties
Oxide layer can be controlled to remain thin and adherent, avoiding spallation
Adaptive tribofilm mechanism operates effectively from RT to 800 °C
